newsitem.title: UK: CZARNIKOW SEES HIGHER WORLD SUGAR OUTPUT IN 97/98.
newsitem.headline: CZARNIKOW SEES HIGHER WORLD SUGAR OUTPUT IN 97/98.

text.p: World sugar production should 123.25 million tonnes raw value in 1997/98, slightly higher than the 123.08 million turned out in 1996/97, Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.
Consumption would rise to 124.37 million tonnes in the 1998 calendar year from 121.96 million, with increased Asian demand the main driving force.

In its first estimate of 1997/98 sugar crops, Czarnikow said output gains that were expected in Brazil, the European Union (EU) and many other producers would be partly offset by a huge decline in India.
Indian production was pegged at 11.69 million tonnes in 1997/98, a fall of 2.23 million from the previous year and more than six million less than only two seasons earlier.
Brazil's output was expected to rise to 15.5 million tonnes from 14.78 million in 1996/97, and EU output would rise to 18.03 million tonnes from 17.98 million.
Cuba would produce 4.00 million tonnes of sugar after 4.2 million, and Thai production would fall by 725,000 tonnes to 5.35 million, based on cane production of 49 million tonnes.
